text:
morgan: Heads up — nightly microbench flagged a regression on candidate kernel build cand-2026-03-15. Looks KV cache peek path for long sequences (>1024) got slower on Ampere variants. CI diff: https://ci.internal/runs/98765 :eyes:

perf-bot: AUTO-ALERT: latency_regression detected (p=0.002). Metric: p50/p95 tail for seq_len=2048 increased by +12% / +27% vs baseline.

morgan: Quick paste from microbench CSV:
```
model,arch,seq_len,p50,p95
llama-70b,ampere,128,16.3,34.2
llama-70b,ampere,1024,21.8,58.4
llama-70b,ampere,2048,44.1,129.3  # REG
llama-70b,h100,2048,36.9,95.1
```

lee: Hmm, that 2048 p95 jump is worrying. Is this on the new merged kv-cache merge? @taylor did the kv cache pointer refactor land in that build?

taylor: yep, landed. The refactor changed when we evict/refresh prefix pages — should be safe but I saw an odd mutex held during async refill in perf lab. I can repro locally with the microprobe harness.

sam: Repro command I used:
```
./microbench --model=llama-70b --arch=ampere --seq=2048 --iters=1000 --kv-mode=peek
```
logs show repeated stall at "kv_fetch_async -> refill_wait".

az: Could be batching heuristic interacting: when seq_len>1024 the runtime switches to "longtail-batch" which changes kv prefetch ordering. If refill waits happen inside the critical path, it will amplify p95.

morgan: Agreed. I ran a quick diff between runtimes: the scheduling decision changed line 243 in batch_planner.cc (new heuristic put 3x larger batches for longtail). Patch attached in CI link.

perf-bot: NOTE: candidate cand-2026-03-15 has kernel selection policy "arch-aware-v2" + batching heuristic "longtail-aggressive". Baseline uses "arch-aware-v1" + "longtail-conservative".

lee: Proposed action list:
- revert longtail-aggressive locally and rerun microbench (taylor)
- add KV refill tracing logs (morgan)
- run night-sweep across Ampere variants w/ seq=[512,1024,1536,2048] (sam)
- mark cand as blocked for autopromote until triage done (perf-bot)


taylor: Starting revert now, will push a quick patch and run smoke. ETA 25m.

morgan: I added tracing snippet:
```
TRACE KV_REFILL start ts=%d nid=%d
TRACE KV_REFILL wait_enter ts=%d
TRACE KV_REFILL wait_exit ts=%d elapsed=%d
```
This should help find whether refill wait is in critical token loop.

sam: Kicked off a focused nightly sweep job with the revert disabled/enabled as separate arms. CI run ids: 98766 (baseline), 98767 (cand+aggressive), 98768 (cand+revert).

ci-bot: Job 98767 finished: failure (p95 regression). Job 98768 finished: success (no regression). Full artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/98767, https://ci.internal/artifacts/98768

morgan: That pretty much nails it — longtail-aggressive interacts poorly with KV refill concurrency on Ampere. Next steps: revert heuristic in cand branch, design a safe concurrency cap for refill, add unit test to microbench harness to cover seq_len 1536/2048.

az: I'll file a follow-up eval to measure cost impact of reverting (expected +3% cost) vs p95 improvements.

lee: Good catch team. Labeling thread: regression-triage/kv-longtail. :thumbsup:"
